issues.what: The ledger-87 vassal land and the Turfan-Hami rectangle (87.5-96.5E, 40-43.5N) tinted about 300 empty desert and mountain cells of Xinjiang as Tang vassal land from 851, and the 850 and 860 Tang keyframes made about 550 cells of Xinjiang direct Tang land in 850-865. Guiyi Circuit page: 'By 850 Zhang had captured Ganzhou, Suzhou, and Yizhou'; 'In 851 Zhang captured Xizhou (Gaochang)'. The event gives the rest of the rectangle to nobody in 851; the keyframes keep only Hami (150 km) and Gaochang (100 km).

qocho-kingdom_860 has Cliopatria interval 860-887 but its own text says 'From 866', with 860-865 covered by the 843-865 keyframe (Karasahr and Kucha only). The compiler started it in 860 (a 1819-cell snap). Now from 866 to 887. Qocho page dates the 843 Uyghur occupation of Karasahr and Kucha.

The Saffarid ledger gains Khorasan in 873 (ledger 8) and loses it only in 900 (ledger 21), but the Cliopatria 896-897 Saffarid shape lacks it, so the 896-899 keyframes cut it (a 1013-cell snap at 898, then unowned land in 898-899). The three Saffarid keyframes now add the Khorasan region, Herat (100 km), Rey (150 km, 898-899) and the Abbasid-Saffarid overlap L43 (898-899); the three Abbasid keyframes cut the same claims (and Persis/Fars in 899) because the R2 successor listing would otherwise give the caliphate every shared cell.

issues.what: Cliopatria's Saffarid shapes of 875-899 reach into Gilgit-Baltistan and northern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (about 250 cells). issues.what: rustamid-dynasty_778 says 'valid 777-811 only' but, with no from/to, took the Cliopatria interval 778-899 and, because the compiler unions every alive keyframe, kept the whole 778 shape (about 1,200 cells too many) through 880-899; rustamid-dynasty_900 ('valid 896-909') started in 900 and left 896-899 to the stale shape. Cell counts after the patch: 538 at 880-895 (was 1742) and 259 at 896-899 (was 1446). Rustamid page: its area contracted to Tahert and its surroundings by the 880s.
principality-of-salerno_840 says 'valid for 861-879' but its Cliopatria interval 840-879 overlapped the 840-850 and 851-860 keyframes, so 61 cells were drawn instead of 11 in 840-850. Now 861-879.

first-bulgarian-empire_850 ('holds 850-855') and _860 ('holds 864-865') overlapped the 856-863 keyframe, so Philippopolis, Zagora and the Burgas ports stayed Bulgarian after the loss of 856 (the compiler unions alive keyframes). Now to 855 and 864-865 (Bulgaria is 1488-1491 cells in 856-863). Boris I page: the peace of late 863 gave Zagora back.

tulunids_878 ('unchanged for 878-897; from 898 see tulunids_898') overlapped tulunids_898, so Aleppo and Qinnasrin (about 100 cells) stayed Tulunid in 898-899 after the treaty of 898. Now to 897 (3278 to 3186 cells in 898-899).

magyars_887 ('holds 887-891, before the Pecheneg advance by 892') overlapped magyars_892, leaving about 400 cells east of the Dnieper to the Magyars in 892-895. Now to 891 (962 cells in 892-894). Pechenegs page dates the advance.

The 898 keyframe of the Kingdom of Italy (an 'ok' Cliopatria shape of the eastern half only, applied at the end of the year) released the 374 cells that ledger 10 gives Berengar in October 898 (the Spoleto-Lombard half, after Lambert's death), leaving a hole at the year end. The keyframe now unions Cliopatria's Kingdom of Italy 898 and 899; the year-end hole goes from 376 to 23 cells and the kingdom from 205 to 579 cells.

The saffarid-dynasty dossier lists the Abbasid caliphate as a successor for Fars from 910 but the listing is undated, so R2 gives the Abbasids every Saffarid conflict cell for the Saffarid's whole life (2965 cell-years remain after the keyframe cuts above).

A scan of the 250 slugs alive in the window found 27 slugs with years in which two keyframes are alive at once, so the snap draws their union. Six were patched above (qocho-kingdom, rustamid-dynasty, principality-of-salerno, first-bulgarian-empire, tulunids, magyars). The other 21 were not opened and their effect in cells was not measured: rashtrakuta-dynasty_806 (819-824), kingdom-of-the-franks_800 and _825 (804-829), viking-settlements_840 and _892 (847-899), pandya-dynasty_592 (100 years, 800-899), kingdom-of-brittany_825 (851-869), aghlabid-dynasty (45 years from 812), champa (75 years, 800-874), kingdom-of-mercia (886-899), balhae (818-824), abbasid-caliphate (837-839), gurjara-pratihara-dynasty (836-839), saffarid-dynasty (864-874), avar-khaganate and obotrites (804-805), east-franks (887-897), great-moravia (890-891), kingdom-of-northumbria (867-869), old-kingdom-of-norway and scandinavian-minor-kingdoms (872-874), mataram-kingdom (898-899), west-franks (879).

Several snaps of Cliopatria shape against ledger state (tulunids_875, tibetans_850, tahirid_821, yufirid_872 and similar) change a few hundred cells at one year end; Great Moravia in 896, the Abbasid holding of Arabia and the Scandinavian umbrella shape read as the dossiers say.
The Emirate of Cordoba shrinks to a remnant of 87 cells in the 890s.
Khorasan in 876-889 stays with the Abbasids in the draft; I did not open pages for who held Nishapur and Herat between 876 and 889.
